mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined for three consecutive weeks (-17.7 to -22.4). This momentum reflects entrenched reduced discretionary activity that will persist without a reversing shock, pushing the next four-week mean further below the last four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell monotonically from -17.7 to -22.4 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean is higher than its last 28-day mean despite three or more prior weeks of monotonic decline.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT usage falls below -20 for two consecutive weeks, reduced public transport trips cut off a key access channel to retail precincts, lowering RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks until transit recovers.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -20 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -20.1 and -20.3 in the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks even though TRANSIT remains below -20 in both preceding weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Joint decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates fewer commuting-linked incidental retail trips (lunch breaks, after-work shopping). The combined suppression of both channels compounds to depress RETAIL_REC more than either series alone would predict, over a four-week horizon.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT declined in each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean does not fall relative to the last 28 days despite concurrent declines in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT exceeding 2 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: During a winter respiratory illness wave, rising RESIDENTIAL alongside sharply falling PARKS signals voluntary self-isolation and risk-avoidance behavior, which suppresses discretionary retail visits over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 6.4 to 8.0 while PARKS fell from -29.3 to -38.9 over the same four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 14-day mean rises despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to climb and PARKS continuing to fall, indicating the isolation mechanism does not transmit to retail behavior.

mechanism_narrative: Winter cold weather in Sydney mechanically reduces outdoor park visits and associated retail stopovers near parks. The steep PARKS decline is a seasonal baseline shift that will continue to depress adjacent retail activity over the coming week regardless of other conditions.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -29.3 to -38.9 over four weeks, consistent with winter seasonality
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the next week while PARKS continues to decline, indicating no seasonal spillover from parks to retail.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES falls by more than 3 points week-on-week alongside a comparable TRANSIT decline, this signals renewed public-health guidance or employer work-from-home policies in response to the winter wave, which will further suppress RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks as overall mobility contracts under policy-driven caution.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 3 points week-on-week while TRANSIT also declines
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -12.3 to -15.1 and TRANSIT fell from -17.3 to -20.3 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 14-day mean increases despite a WORKPLACES week-on-week decline exceeding 3 points, indicating no policy-driven suppression transmission.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has declined less steeply than RETAIL_REC across all four weeks, indicating households are prioritizing essential shopping while cutting discretionary retail trips. This substitution pattern, if it persists, predicts continued relative suppression of RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:the gap between RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM widened from -6.3 to -7.8 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean rises relative to GROCERY_PHARM's trend, narrowing or reversing the gap, contradicting the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: Once PARKS drops below -35, a cold-snap threshold is crossed that sharply curtails foot traffic to retail precincts co-located with outdoor recreation areas, producing an immediate one-week drag on RETAIL_REC before any recovery.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached -36.9 and -38.9 in the last two weeks, crossing the -35 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 7-day mean does not fall relative to the prior week despite PARKS remaining below -35.
